findings.title: Missing `paths`/`paths-ignore` on Expensive Workflows
findings.evidence: workflow triggers on pull_request/push but declares no `paths:`/`paths-ignore:` filter (the `on:` block below has no `paths:` key). NOTE: if this workflow is a REQUIRED status check, add a per-job `dorny/paths-filter` gate that returns a neutral pass — a workflow-level `paths:` filter would strand the required check on excluded PRs.
findings.size_note: below the cluster floor — runner-minute (bill) only, no wall-clock
findings.runner_min_note: gross upper bound — assumes every irrelevant run runs the full job and a `paths:` filter skips it; realizable only where the workflow's jobs don't ALREADY self-skip (via `if:` guards or an internal change-gate) and the trigger can be narrowed safely — verify per workflow before crediting

findings.title: No Draft PR Gating on Expensive Jobs
findings.evidence: expensive job `tests` (matrix) runs on every PR that changes the workflow's filtered `paths:` including drafts — no `if: github.event.pull_request.draft == false` gate
findings.size_note: per-job runner-minutes not sized — this finding skips a single job, but that job's duration couldn't be resolved from sampled run timings (reusable-workflow caller or name-overridden job); saving ≈ the job's own minutes × skip-rate × volume

findings.title: Cron Schedule Too Frequent
findings.evidence: 95 scheduled run(s) in 5 consecutive same-head_sha group(s) re-ran without a code change in the sampled schedule slice (95% of 100 schedule run(s)); ~3 runner-min/mo of schedule-event compute (mean over 20 timed run(s); ×0.30 to the 30d volume (30 runs); 100-run recent slice (not a full 30d census)).
findings.measured_signal: event=schedule total_count x mean job-minutes (30 schedule run(s)/30d; 95 same-head_sha redundant run(s); 20 timed run(s); scale 0.3)
findings.size_note: runner-minute (bill) only — schedule-event runs do not gate a PR; frequency change must preserve any operational cadence requirement.

measured_evidence.summary: 95 scheduled run(s) in 5 consecutive same-head_sha group(s) re-ran without a code change in the sampled schedule slice (95% of 100 schedule run(s)); ~3 runner-min/mo of schedule-event compute (mean over 20 timed run(s); ×0.30 to the 30d volume (30 runs); 100-run recent slice (not a full 30d census)).
measured_evidence.note: Schedule burn is counted only on event=schedule runs whose head_sha repeats consecutively, so the detector proves the workflow ran again without a code change. Basis: the count is from the all-status schedule slice; the per-run price is the mean of 20 successful schedule-event timed run(s). GUARDRAIL: confirm the current cadence is not an operational SLA before increasing the cron interval.

tier2_neutrality.ref: event=schedule subset only; consecutive same-head_sha schedule runs; schedule is not a developer PR/merge event

findings.guardrail: Confirm the cron cadence is not an operational SLA; prefer widening the interval only for cleanup/triage/build jobs where delayed execution is acceptable.
findings.runner_min_door_note: modeled static estimate (default_s / hit_rate), disclosed as modeled in the report's sized-of-total ratio — not a spine-billable derivation
